newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Sofia American bar serves sandwiches to protesters.
newsitem.headline: Sofia American bar serves sandwiches to protesters.

text.p: A New York-style bar in the Bulgarian capital is serving free tea and sandwiches in a gesture of support for opposition protesters who are massed outside parliament to back demands for a general election.

"These people stood out there for over 14 hours yesterday, doing what the politicians told them to," said Californian Philip Bay, owner of Radio City New York, a 1930s-themed bar near the parliament buildings. "It's not fair to tell people to stay home and not continue to protest."
He said Radio City had started on Saturday evening to hand out ham and cheese sandwiches with mayonnaise and mustard.

Private art galleries near the parliament served free tea and coffee on Friday and supporters brought food and drinks to sustain the demonstrators who blockaded parliament in freezing temperatures until they were dispersed by riot police early on Saturday.
By mid-morning they were back in place but the ex-communist ruling Socialist party showed no sign of yielding to pressure.
